**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**
The test image shows a single mango leaf that is:
- Partially green with prominent brown, ragged/necrotic margins
- Curled and crumpled in texture
- Young leaf with irregular torn-looking edges, especially along the margins

**Candidate Narrowing:**
- **Anthracnose**: Matches well — "semicircular lesions on margins of young leaves," curled/crumpled brown appearance
- **Cutting_Weevil**: Reference shows much more severe stripping — bare stems with only tiny stubs remaining; test leaf retains most of its blade
- **Die_Back**: Reference shows completely brown/dried shriveled leaves — more advanced desiccation than test image
- **Gall_Midge**: Shows round blister galls on an otherwise intact leaf surface — not matching
- **Sooty_Mould / Powdery_Mildew**: Show surface coatings (black/white), not margin necrosis

**Conclusion:** The test leaf's brown necrotic margins, curled young leaf appearance, and partially intact green blade matches the Anthracnose pattern of "semicircular lesions on margins of young leaves" most closely. The Anthracnose reference images (top-right panel especially) show the same brown/curled young leaf morphology.
